title: Influence of Chitosan on the Protective Properties of ZrO2 – Based Multilayer Hybrid System on Low Carbon Steel
content: The manuscript demonstrates a new approach to improve and evaluate the effect of chitosan (CS) underlayer on the protective properties of ZrO2 sol gel films, deposited on galvanized low carbon steel. In order to obtain more optimized results chitosan was dissolved in citric acid leading to appearance of chitosan-based solution accompanied with crosslinking of the polymer. Two manners of treatment of chitosan underlayer have been applied – drying at ambient temperature or processing at higher temperatures for a definite time interval. Thereafter, the experimental samples with deposited CS layer, were subsequently immersed into zirconium precursor solution and finally treated in air at 180oC. Several methods such as X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), water contact angle (CA) and X-ray Photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) were applied to examine the properties of the newly developed hybrid systems. The corrosion parameters and protective ability of the latter were evaluated by means of potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves in a model corrosive medium of 5% NaCl. The results obtained confirmed the positive effect of chitosan on the corrosion resistance of the hybrid protective system in aggressive medium containing chloride ions as corrosion activators.
